summary: Sillon, developed by Soil AI Crew, is an intelligent web application designed to optimize precision agriculture and combat food insecurity. By combining satellite data analysis with machine learning models, the platform assesses soil health and predicts optimal agronomic conditions. It provides farmers and rural development stakeholders with accurate diagnostic tools to monitor crops, recommend targeted corrective actions, and anticipate climatic or environmental changes. Through this AI-driven technological approach, Soil AI Crew helps maximize agricultural yields while preserving natural resources.
details:
1. What does it do / How does it work?

Sillon is an intelligent web application designed to optimize precision agriculture and combat food insecurity. The platform integrates satellite data analysis with advanced machine learning models to assess real-time soil health and predict optimal agronomic conditions. Users can interact with the web interface to monitor crop zones, analyze soil parameters, and receive automated, data-driven diagnostic insights.

2. What are the benefits?

  • Precision Farming: Provides farmers and rural stakeholders with precise, actionable diagnostic tools instead of guesswork.
  • Proactive Decision-Making: Helps identify environmental stresses and nutrient deficiencies early.
  • Resource Optimization: Promotes sustainable farming practices by maximizing agricultural yields while conserving vital natural resources like water and soil integrity.

3. What is the expected impact of the project?

Sillon empowers local farmers, agronomists, and communities to adapt to changing climatic conditions. By improving agricultural efficiency and crop resilience, the project directly contributes to long-term food security, reduces economic losses for smallholder farmers, and fosters sustainable rural development in regions vulnerable to climate shifts.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Frontend / Deployment: Hosted live on Vercel (https://soil-ai-sandy.vercel.app), ensuring fast, reliable, and public access for judges.
  • Version Control & Collaboration: Managed via GitHub repository.
  • Core Technologies: Web development frameworks (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/React), paired with machine learning models and geospatial/satellite data integration pipelines.

5. How is your project creative?

Sillon creatively bridges complex space-based Earth observation data and machine learning with everyday agricultural needs. Rather than presenting raw satellite data that is difficult for a regular farmer to interpret, Sillon translates these advanced analytics into an intuitive, accessible web application that delivers instant, localized agronomic recommendations.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Accessibility & Usability: Designed a clean, responsive user interface ensuring the platform is easy to use for anyone involved in agricultural planning.
  • Real-World Viability: Focused heavily on solving real, urgent challenges related to food security and sustainable resource management in developing regions.
  • Scalability: Built a lightweight web architecture capable of scaling to process broader geographical datasets and regional crop monitoring.

dataRefs: NASA POWER (rainfall, min/max/mean temperature, surface soil moisture, 10 years of daily data)
NASA GIBS, MODIS Terra (daily true-colour satellite imagery at 250 m, used as the Earth-observation basemap)
NASA SRTM (elevation and slope, used for erosion risk)
projectRefs: ERA5 / ERA5-Land, Copernicus / ECMWF (reference evapotranspiration, 0–7 cm soil moisture)
USGS 3DEP (elevation at 5 points around the site, used to compute slope)
SoilGrids 2.0, ISRIC (texture, carbon, pH, water retention, WRB soil class, 0–60 cm)
Open-Meteo (access to ERA5 archives, 14-day forecasts, elevation and place search)
Google Maps JavaScript API (satellite basemap, point selection)
